name: Kei
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_quote: Stress always falls on the final syllable. Only some words that have been taken from Malay are an exception to this rule. When suffixes are added to a word the stress falls on the suffix that is the final syllable of the derived word. In words with more than two syllables the first syllable is also stressed, but the final syllable bears the strongest stress. (Geurtjens 1922)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict final (stress placement coded per word length as 01 101 1001 (1 = a stressed syllable)) rests on Travis 1990, a dedicated 58-pp SIL phonological description, quoted verbatim at pp. 7-8 in the copy consulted, and is independently confirmed by Tetelepta 1985:21 (held), Travis 1993 (held), van Engelenhoven 2021:394 (held, 'iambic', final main stress) and now the Geurtjens 1921:7 Dutch original downloaded from archive.org, which matches the StressTyp2 paraphrase in the domain quotation. No better description exists in Glottolog's list. The record's grade/quote/cite fields are blank even though primary quotes are held and verified, so the action is to fill the grade (primary, verified) and move the Travis quote into quote/cite/loc. Two nuances worth a caution line but not a reclassify: (a) Travis type II groups (host+enclitic, a few irregular inalienably possessed nouns in -r-in, Malay loans) have penultimate stress, and Geurtjens lists unstressed -se/-le; thes

sources.quote: 'De klemtoon valt altijd op de laatste lettergreep.' Exceptions: a few words taken over (nearly) unchanged from Malay; suffixes attract stress as the new final syllable except diminutive -se and -le which stay unstressed (denkoet-se, wekat-le); in words of more than two syllables the first syllable also gets more emphasis but the heaviest stress stays final; clipped dialect forms re-stress the new final syllable; Atnebar/Kei-Tanimbar speakers (of Fordata origin) stress the penult; p. 8: 'in de Keieesche taal de klemtoon slechts van ondergeschikt belang is'.
sources.locator: p. 7-8, section 'KLEMTOON' (leaf 77-78 of the archive.org scan)
